LESSON: READING 13.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: PRAISE SONGS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we sing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed
2. discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs
3. perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment
4. appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 13.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: PRAISE SONGS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 13.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: PRAISE SONGS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment

What this means
In this part you learn to perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs to a partner. (skill: discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the purpose of praise songs in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed.
3. Practise this skill: discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs.
4. Practise this skill: perform praise songs sung in their immediate environment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we sing?
2. What are the qualities of a good singer?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the purpose and occasions for which praise songs are performed.
5. Be able to: discuss the relationship between the singer and the person being praised in praise songs.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
